land.text: 'established in 1500 in the centre of the Holy Roman Empire'

predecessors.note: The circle is an association of the Empire's estates, never territory (rule 4).

correction.text: the member territories of the Franconian Circle: Bamberg, Wurzburg, Eichstatt, Ansbach, Bayreuth, Nuremberg, the Teutonic Order's Franconian bailiwick, Hohenlohe, Schwarzenberg, Castell, Wertheim and Henneberg; the gazetteer's Franconia region is a coarse stand-in

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for an association, never coloured as territory (rule 4). The page gives no area or population; it lists 25 members in a table (the Reichstag seats of Bamberg 11th, Eichstatt 17th, Ansbach 28th, Bayreuth 30th, the Teutonic Order 9th). The stand-in is the gazetteer's Franconia region (about 38,200 km2), which also holds Hohenlohe and other lands of the circle; Eichstatt and the Teutonic Order's Mergentheim may lie partly outside it.

ledger.note: 2 July 1500: the Franconian Circle was 'established in 1500 in the centre of the Holy Roman Empire' (infobox 'Established: 1500'; the page dates the Reichstag of Augsburg's division to '2 July 1500'). Review follow-up: the counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259; changed to holy-roman-empire-minor-states (Cliopatria's 1260..1806 row).

1806: the circle ends with the Empire (infobox 'Disestablished: 1806'). The page does not describe the end beyond the infobox; Ansbach had passed to Prussia in 1791 ('Established in 1398 and acquired by Prussia in 1791'). Review follow-up: the counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259; changed to holy-roman-empire-minor-states (Cliopatria's 1260..1806 row).

certainty.note: An association of estates; the page gives a member table and no territory or area.

sources.title: Franconian Circle
sources.note: Established 1500, Reichstag of Augsburg 2 July 1500; 25 members; Ansbach to Prussia 1791; infobox disestablished 1806.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New association (type umbrella), named in the brief's scope. Rule 4: never territory; the member lands with their own dossiers in this batch (Bamberg, Wurzburg, Ansbach, Bayreuth) carry the land.

SHAPE. The gazetteer's Franconia region (about 38,200 km2). The page gives no area and no population, and not the directors or the seat of the circle's diet (Nuremberg appears only as a member imperial city), so no capital is entered.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No area; (2) the page's table lists 25 members and no total; (3) no war or military event on the page (it mentions only a Landfrieden union that 'disintegrated in the face of opposition from cities and princes').

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new (Eichstatt, Nuremberg and the Teutonic Order's bailiwick are not written here).

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). The reviewer failed this dossier because its type is umbrella: an Imperial Circle is an association of estates, never territory (brief rule 4), and its shape overlays the member states that have dossiers of their own. That is an orchestrator decision (drop the file, or keep it only if the compiler skips type umbrella); the brief for this batch asked for the circle and rule 4 says 'type: umbrella for associations', so the file is left in place and its type unchanged. The only change made: the found and dissolve counterpart holy-roman-empire (dossier ends 1259) is now holy-roman-empire-minor-states. NOT CHANGED: the shape (a coarse stand-in laid over the member states' own dossiers).
